Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Inherent Disagreements in Human Textual Inferences (ACL-Anthology-Q19-1043-captured-copy) · paper method: After removing specified outlier/sparse workers, does-not-make-sense responses and pairs with fewer than 15 remaining judgments, the analysis retained 496 pairs averaging 39 labels each; ratings were z-normalized within each worker assignment, not globally across pairs.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Inherent Disagreements in Human Textual Inferences (ACL-Anthology-Q19-1043-captured-copy) · paper method: The authors explicitly state that z-normalized scores are not comparable across batches because batches contain different sentence pairs; their within-pair analysis depends on comparing raters for the same pair rather than interpreting one universal numeric scale.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Inherent Disagreements in Human Textual Inferences (ACL-Anthology-Q19-1043-captured-copy) · paper method: The study sampled 100 premise/hypothesis pairs from each of RTE2, SNLI, MNLI, JOCI and DNC, requiring each sentence to be at most 20 words, and requested 50 independent AMT ratings per pair on a −50 to 50 likelihood slider.

cohort9.claim.inherent.sampling

  • Recruitment required at least 98% AMT approval and 100 approved HITs, residence in the US, Canada, UK, Australia or New Zealand, and paid $0.30 per 20-pair batch.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Inherent Disagreements in Human Textual Inferences (ACL-Anthology-Q19-1043-captured-copy) · paper method: With ten held-out judgments per pair and results averaged over ten random splits, a fitted Gaussian-mixture analysis found a second component of weight above 0.2 for about 20% of sentence pairs; most pairs were consistent with a single component.

cohort9.claim.inherent.secondary-mode

  • This is a model-based characterization of the collected normalized judgments, not a verified universal fraction of linguistic ambiguity.
